notes.f1: True match: Moe Parauhia (97XW-7VN), son of Parauhia Paura and Paerai Teupooihi, married Aufait/Aufaite Toehae (the Aufait/Aufaite spelling is the documented index variation). The spouse relationship is supported by the record evidence the run actually captured — two distinct indexed civil-registration marriage entries (src_001 = ark:/61903/1:1:D955-NRW2, Teavaro; src_002 = ark:/61903/1:1:QTBT-LJMM, Teaharoa), each naming Moe and Aufaite Toehae in 1860 — together with a birth registration (ark:/61903/1:1:D71K-HMT2) and the parents matching the tree couple (LCX2-L8S / LCX2-LKN). The two marriage entries are separate index records on two Moorea communes (Teavaro vs Teaharoa); that place difference is not reconciled by any extracted assertion. No extracted assertion carries a witness, registrar, or officiant, so the two acts are not established as independently produced records, and I do not treat them as independent corroboration on that basis. No original page image was examined (full-text is non-functional for this collection). Proof quality = 2 (thin) under the current rubric: the evidence is useful and corroborative and the identification is well-anchored, but the "proved"-tier reasoning rests on an independence claim the extracted evidence does not establish, and the Teavaro/Teaharoa difference is an unreconciled place discrepancy not captured as a resolved conflict — so the soundness is thin rather than sound.
